Login.// note: docker-compose.yml runs the backend with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development, so this block — not appsettings.json — is the value actually in force under docker compose up. Keep it in sync with the base file (60/60s per ADR-0016).

PublicApply.// note: Same as Login above: this is the value the compose deployment actually uses. Higher than login because a shared job link produces a genuine burst from one NAT address.

AI.// note: Local development only. With no key the endpoints answer from canned samples so the Candidate 360 UI is drivable offline; every such response carries X-Ai-Simulated: true. Set a real ApiKey here to exercise the providers — the stubs then stop applying entirely, and provider errors surface as 502.

Smtp.// note: Local development writes .eml files instead of connecting to a server. This is NOT a stub in the sense the AI fallback above is: the real renderer runs and the real message is written, so what you open in ./tmp/mail is byte-for-byte what a candidate would have received. Nothing is fabricated and nothing claims to have been delivered. Set Host (and clear PickupDirectory) to exercise a real relay — MailHog on localhost:1025 works with UseStartTls false.
